articles.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
articles.text:
Google will now allow you to remove visible watermarks from the images, videos, and music made with AI tools. With the update, you can toggle off a new “Media watermark” setting in Gemini and Google’s AI video generator, Flow.
You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
Google will still embed invisible SynthID and C2PA watermarks into AI-generated images, videos, and music.
When toggled off, Google will remove the “sparkle” watermark that appears in the bottom-right corner of content generated with the company’s Nano Banana and Omni models. Though visible watermarks are now optional, AI-generated content will have invisible SynthID watermarks and C2PA metadata embedded in the background, according to Josh Woodward, the vice president of Google Labs, Gemini, and AI Studio. That means you can still verify if a piece of content has one of these markers by asking Gemini or Search if it’s AI-generated.
While this change might make it more difficult to quickly discern if an image or video is AI-generated, many users have already been editing out visible watermarks. Other AI image generators, like OpenAI and Meta’s, also don’t apply visible watermarks. Instead, OpenAI relies on SynthID and C2PA to signal whether something is AI-generated, while Meta launched its own Content Seal standard. Anthropic also announced this week that it’s applying invisible watermarks to both AI-generated text and images.
Google plans on rolling out its new watermark setting to Search as well, but the toggle won’t launch in countries that require visible watermarks.

articles.title: Las mejores series españolas de humor en Netflix (Agosto 2026)
articles.text:
La comedia es el género que mejor ha resistido el salto de la televisión en abierto al streaming, y el catálogo español de la plataforma lo confirma. Esta selección reúne ocho series españolas de humor en Netflix que van del falso documental al sainete funerario, pasando por la parodia de superhéroes y la comedia romántica de media hora. Varias figuran también en la selección general de las mejores series españolas en Netflix, que aquí se filtra por un criterio único, hacer reír.
Hay un apellido que aparece dos veces, el de los hermanos Alberto y Laura Caballero, responsables de la factoría que ha convertido el humor coral y de portal en un formato reconocible dentro y fuera de España. El resto llega de orígenes muy distintos, del teatro, del cómic, de la novela y hasta de una broma en redes sociales. Casi todas caben en episodios de menos de media hora y la mayoría tiene ya su final escrito, algo que agradecerá quien busque reírse sin comprometerse a nada largo.
Machos alfa (2022)
Género Comedia. Nota FilmAffinity 6,3. Temporadas 5. Episodios 42.
Los hermanos Caballero llevan dos décadas destilando el sainete español en clave de sitcom y aquí aplican esa maquinaria a la crisis de la masculinidad. Pedro, Santi, Raúl y Luis son cuatro cuarentones que descubren de golpe que el mundo ha dejado de estar diseñado a su medida y deciden reeducarse, con resultados que nunca son los previstos. El mecanismo cómico vive en la distancia entre lo que los personajes creen estar haciendo y lo que ve el espectador, un desajuste que Machos alfa sostiene durante cinco temporadas sin sermonear a nadie. Las réplicas van rápidas, el reparto funciona como conjunto y el humor incomoda lo justo. Ha encontrado público muy lejos de España, en países donde ese debate suena distinto.
Creada por Alberto Caballero y Laura Caballero. Con Fernando Gil, María Hervás, Raúl Tejón, Kira Miró, Gorka Otxoa y Fele Martínez.
Paquita Salas (2016-2019)
Género Comedia. Nota FilmAffinity 7,2. Temporadas 3. Episodios 16.
Nació como una broma en redes sociales y acabó siendo una de las series españolas de humor en Netflix con más frases incrustadas en el habla común. Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi escogieron la forma del falso documental para retratar a una representante de actores que sigue operando con los códigos de los años noventa mientras la industria se le escapa entre los dedos. Brays Efe sostiene a Paquita Salas sin caricaturizarla, acompañado de una ayudante que empeora todo lo que toca y de una mánager con más ambición que escrúpulos, capaces de robar cada escena que pisan. El conjunto acumuló cuatro premios Feroz y un Ondas. Dieciséis episodios cortos bastan para entender por qué se cita de memoria.
Creada por Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi. Con Brays Efe, Belén Cuesta, Lidia San José y Anna Castillo.
Muertos S.L. (2024-2026)
Género Comedia, comedia negra. Nota FilmAffinity 6,7. Temporadas 4. Episodios 26.
La muerte del fundador de la funeraria Torregrosa deja el negocio sin sucesor claro y ahí arranca todo. Dámaso Carrillo, comercial de la casa y mano derecha del difunto, da por hecho que el puesto le pertenece, pero la viuda decide ponerse al frente con la ayuda de un yerno entusiasta y del todo inútil que se presenta como experto en marketing. Carlos Areces construye un jefe pomposo e insufrible al que resulta imposible dejar de mirar, y el tanatorio convierte a Muertos S.L. en terreno fértil para el humor negro porque impone solemnidad justo cuando los personajes menos pueden sostenerla. La serie concluyó en su cuarta temporada, de modo que el maratón llega con desenlace incluido.
Creada por Alberto Caballero, Laura Caballero, Daniel Deorador y Julián Sastre. Con Carlos Areces, Ascen López, Diego Martín, Salva Reina, Amaia Salamanca y Aitziber Garmendia.
Animal (2025)
Género Comedia, vida rural. Nota FilmAffinity 6,3. Temporadas 1. Episodios 9.
Luis Zahera lleva años interpretando a hombres duros y aquí desmonta ese registro sin renunciar al mal genio. Antón es un veterinario rural gallego al que los vecinos pagan con huevos y favores, hasta que las facturas lo empujan a aceptar un empleo en la boutique de mascotas que dirige su sobrina Uxía. El choque entre quien ha pasado la vida entre vacas y una clientela urbana que trata a sus perros como hijos alimenta un contraste que Animal explota con más paciencia que estridencia. Dentro de las series españolas de humor en Netflix es la más apegada al territorio, con nueve capítulos de menos de media hora rodados en un pueblo gallego inventado y un paisaje que actúa de personaje.
Creada por Víctor García León. Con Luis Zahera, Lucía Caraballo, Carmen Ruiz, Antonio Durán Morris y Nuno Gallego.
El vecino (2019-2021)
Género Comedia, fantástico. Nota FilmAffinity 5,6. Temporadas 2. Episodios 18.
El relato de superhéroes suele empezar con alguien digno del poder que recibe. Aquí sucede al revés. Javier es un treintañero incapaz de ordenar su propia vida cuando hereda por accidente las facultades de un alienígena, y la comedia sale de todo lo que un traje de licra no arregla, desde el alquiler hasta la pareja. Parte del cómic firmado por Santiago García y Pepo Pérez, El vecino renuncia al espectáculo y se queda a la escala del portal y del ascensor, un terreno donde Quim Gutiérrez y Clara Lago se mueven con soltura. Dieciocho capítulos repartidos en dos temporadas que cerraron la historia sin estirarla más de lo necesario.
Creada por Miguel Esteban y Raúl Navarro. Con Quim Gutiérrez, Clara Lago, Adrián Pino y Catalina Sopelana.
Smiley (2022)
Género Comedia romántica. Nota FilmAffinity 6,4. Temporadas 1. Episodios 8.
Media hora por capítulo, Barcelona en Navidad y una comedia romántica que no disimula su mecánica de vodevil. Un mensaje de voz enviado al número equivocado pone en contacto a un camarero y a un arquitecto que no coinciden en casi nada, y de ese error nace en Smiley una relación que ninguno de los dos había planeado. Guillem Clua adapta su propia obra teatral y conserva el pulso de las réplicas, con Carlos Cuevas y Miki Esparbé llevando el peso mientras alrededor se despliegan otras parejas en momentos muy distintos de su vida. Es la más navideña de estas series españolas de humor en Netflix y se resuelve en ocho episodios de una única temporada, un formato pensado para una sola noche.
Creada por Guillem Clua. Con Carlos Cuevas, Miki Esparbé, Pepón Nieto y Meritxell Calvo.
Un cuento perfecto (2023)
Género Comedia romántica. Nota FilmAffinity 6,2. Temporadas 1. Episodios 5.
Margot abandona su boda minutos antes de la ceremonia y David reparte el día entre varios empleos mal pagados. El azar los cruza y sellan un acuerdo, cada uno ayudará al otro a recuperar la relación que ha perdido, con la certeza absoluta de que entre ellos no va a ocurrir nada. Ese trato es maquinaria clásica de la comedia romántica y Un cuento perfecto lo asume sin complejos, aprovechando la diferencia de clase entre ambos para sacar chispas de cada escena compartida. Anna Castillo y Álvaro Mel se entienden en pantalla y cinco capítulos luminosos bastan para cerrarlo, la propuesta más breve de toda la selección.
Dirigida por Chloé Wallace. Con Anna Castillo, Álvaro Mel, Ana Belén e Ingrid García Jonsson.
Valeria (2020-2025)
Género Comedia romántica, drama. Nota FilmAffinity 4,8. Temporadas 4. Episodios 30.
Diana Gómez, Silma López, Paula Malia y Teresa Riott forman el cuarteto que carga con esta comedia y explica buena parte de su interés. Valeria es una escritora bloqueada cuyo matrimonio se desmorona, y las conversaciones con sus tres amigas acaban siendo el verdadero motor del relato, entre confidencias, decisiones malas y humor de sobremesa. Es la propuesta más ligera de estas series españolas de humor en Netflix y también la que menos convence a los votantes de FilmAffinity, con una nota bastante por debajo del resto de la lista. Cumple, eso sí, lo que promete cuando el plan es una tarde sin exigencias. La cuarta temporada puso punto final en 2025 y dejó atados los frentes sentimentales de la protagonista.
Creada por María López Castaño. Con Diana Gómez, Silma López, Paula Malia, Teresa Riott y Maxi Iglesias.
¿Por dónde empezar tu maratón de comedia española en Netflix?
Si buscas el humor más afilado y no te asusta reírte de lo que en principio no debería tener gracia, empieza por Muertos S.L. y su funeraria en guerra permanente. Si prefieres algo que se cite de memoria y se termine en una tarde, Paquita Salas es la puerta de entrada evidente a las series españolas de humor en Netflix, con capítulos breves y un personaje que ya forma parte del imaginario común. Y si lo que te apetece es comedia con paisaje y mal genio, Animal deja mejor cuerpo que cualquier maratón largo. Ninguna de las tres exige compromiso, que es justo lo que se le pide a una comedia.

articles.title: Redmi 14C vs 15C: Price, specs and buying guide
articles.text:
Table of contents
The Redmi 14C and Redmi 15C are Xiaomi’s budget phones in the C series, released a year apart. Both phones share the same MediaTek Helio G81 Ultra chipset. The main differences are in battery, charging speed, durability, screen brightness, and camera.
This guide compares their prices, specs, and features so you can decide which one offers better value for your money.
Redmi 14C vs 15C price in Nigeria
Prices for both phones change frequently due to the naira-to-dollar exchange rate. Store prices also differ, so treat these figures as a guide rather than fixed.
Redmi 15C prices (by RAM and storage):
- 4GB/128GB: from ₦130,900 up to ₦173,013, depending on the store
- 6GB/128GB: from ₦143,900 up to ₦199,300
- 8GB/256GB: from ₦168,900 up to ₦230,806
Redmi 14C prices (by RAM and storage):
- 4GB/128GB: from ₦125,600 up to ₦134,900
- 6GB/128GB: from ₦142,600 up to ₦146,600
- 8GB/256GB: from ₦157,600 up to ₦162,600
Stock levels matter too. The Redmi 14C is getting harder to find, especially on Jumia, and some stores now sell it as limited stock or as a UK-used unit. The Redmi 15C is widely available brand-new on Jumia, Slot, Konga, and Jiji.
On average, the Redmi 15C costs about ₦15,000 to ₦40,000 more than the Redmi 14C for the same RAM and storage.
Redmi 14C vs 15C specs compared
1. Design and build
- The Redmi 14C measures 171.9 x 77.8 x 8.2mm and weighs between 204g and 211g, depending on the colour.
- The Redmi 15C measures 171.6 x 79.5 x 8.0mm and weighs 205g.
- The Redmi 14C carries an IP52 rating, which protects it from light splashes and dust.
- The Redmi 15C carries an IP64 rating, which protects it from dust and stronger water splashes. This is a genuine upgrade in durability.
2. Display
- Both phones use a 120Hz IPS LCD screen.
- The Redmi 14C has a 6.88-inch display with a resolution of 720 x 1640 pixels.
- The Redmi 15C has a slightly bigger 6.9-inch display with a resolution of 720 x 1600 pixels.
- The Redmi 15C is brighter. It reaches up to 810 nits at peak brightness, while the Redmi 14C peaks at 600 nits.
3. Performance
Both phones run on the same MediaTek Helio G81 Ultra chipset, paired with an octa-core CPU and a Mali-G52 MC2 GPU. You should not expect any speed improvements when moving from the Redmi 14C to the Redmi 15C.
Storage and RAM options are close as well:
- Redmi 14C: 4GB/64GB, 4GB/128GB, 6GB/128GB, 8GB/128GB, 4GB/256GB, and 8GB/256GB
- Redmi 15C: 4GB/128GB, 6GB/128GB, 8GB/128GB, 4GB/256GB, and 8GB/256GB
Both phones support memory extension up to 16GB and have a dedicated microSD card slot for extra storage.
4. Camera
Both phones have a 50MP main rear camera with an extra depth lens. This is where the comparison flips in favour of the older phone.
- The Redmi 14C has a 13MP selfie camera.
- The Redmi 15C has an 8MP selfie camera.
This means the Redmi 15C took a step back in the front-camera department. If selfies and video calls matter to you, factor this into your decision.
5. Battery and charging
- The Redmi 14C has a 5,160mAh battery with 18W charging.
- The Redmi 15C has a 6,000mAh battery with 33W charging.
This is the biggest upgrade the Redmi 15C offers. You get a larger battery and much faster charging. Neither phone comes with a charger in the box, so you will need a compatible charger if you don’t already have one.
6. Software and updates
- The Redmi 14C ships with Android 14 on HyperOS and gets 2 major OS upgrades plus 4 years of security updates.
- The Redmi 15C ships with Android 15 on HyperOS 2 and gets 4 major OS upgrades plus 6 years of security updates.
This means the Redmi 15C will be supported longer, which matters if you plan to keep your phone for several years.
Full specs comparison

Which one should you buy?
Pick the Redmi 15C if you want a bigger battery, faster charging, better durability, and longer software support. Most buyers should go with the Redmi 15C, since it costs a little more but offers better long-term value.
Pick the Redmi 14C if you find it at a noticeably lower price, or if the better selfie camera matters more to you than battery life.
Neither phone will feel faster than the other, since they share the same chipset. If performance and smooth multitasking matter most, choose the 6GB or 8GB RAM option on either phone instead of paying more for the newer model.

You can buy the Redmi 15C brand new from Jumia, Slot, Konga, and Jiji. It is also available in physical stores across Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Port Harcourt, Kano, Kaduna, and Ibadan.
The Redmi 14C is still available on Slot, Konga, and Jiji, both new and UK-used. Stock is limited on some platforms, and Jumia currently does not list it.

articles.title: Google Meet utilise désormais Gemini pour prendre des notes lors de vos réunions physiques
articles.text:
La prise de notes automatique par IA, Google l’a d’abord réservée aux visioconférences. Le principe : Gemini écoute la réunion, la transcrit et en sort un résumé écrit à la fin. Jusqu’ici, il fallait être en appel vidéo pour en profiter. Ce n’est plus le cas, comme l’a repéré Android Authority.
Gemini prend des notes même sans caméra
Concrètement, la fonction se lance depuis l’application mobile Meet. Vous démarrez une session de prise de notes pour une réunion qui se déroule dans une salle, sans appel vidéo. Le micro du téléphone capte les échanges, Gemini les transcrit puis génère un compte rendu que vous récupérez après coup. Plus besoin de désigner quelqu’un pour gribouiller les décisions sur un carnet.
Cette extension s’inscrit dans la même logique que les autres évolutions récentes de l’outil, entre sa nouvelle page d’accueil côté web et son arrivée sur Android Auto. Google pousse Meet partout, et surtout Gemini avec, comme il le fait déjà dans Gmail et Docs.
La fonction reste cependant liée aux abonnements Google Workspace donnant accès à Gemini. Cet outil est taillé pour les entreprises et les équipes. Pour ceux qui enchaînent les réunions en salle, ça évite de choisir entre suivre la discussion et tout noter.

articles.title: Microsoft commence ses travaux vers une app Copilot unifiée
articles.text:
Microsoft a détaillé la fusion entre son application Copilot grand public et Microsoft 365 Copilot, réunies dans une seule interface qui reprend le nom "Microsoft Copilot". L'éditeur prépare le terrain pour sa superapp promise par Satya Nadella fin juillet dernier.
Nous rapportions fin juillet que le patron de Microsoft avait confirmé son intention de réunir chat, code et agents autonomes dans une seule "super-application". Les premiers changements concrets démarrent cette semaine, avec un calendrier de déploiement qui s'étale jusqu'à la mi-septembre.
Une interface commune, des comptes qui restent cloisonnés
Concrètement, les utilisateurs de l'application Copilot grand public (connectés via un compte Microsoft, Google ou Apple) seront migrés vers cette nouvelle version, tout en conservant leurs conversations et leurs fichiers. De leur côté, les utilisateurs de Microsoft 365 Copilot verront leur application renommée, avec une nouvelle icône et un accès gratuit au chat Copilot. À l'heure actuelle, ce dernier est réservé à certains abonnements professionnels. Si un même compte personnel utilisait les deux applications, son contenu serait regroupé dans l'application unifiée.
Cette fusion ne mélange toutefois pas les usages personnels et professionnels. Un compte "Microsoft Entra" (le système d'identité utilisé par les entreprises et les établissements scolaires) reste distinct d'un compte Microsoft classique. Les données saisies côté professionnel ne circuleront donc pas vers le compte personnel, et inversement. Microsoft précise également qu'aucune modification n'affecte les contrôles de sécurité, de confidentialité, de conformité et d'administration déjà en place pour les organisations.
Certains testeurs Windows Insiders reçoivent déjà la mise à jour cette semaine, avant un lancement global des versions mobile et web à la mi-août, puis des applications Windows et Mac à la mi-septembre. Les fichiers partagés ou créés dans l'application Copilot autonome seront par ailleurs stockés dans OneDrive.
Plusieurs fonctions disparaissent au passage. C'est le cas des podcasts générés par l'IA, l'outil de recherche approfondie ("Deep Research") et les discussions de groupe qui ne seront plus accessibles après le 18 août 2026. L'éditeur recommande ainsi aux utilisateurs concernés d'exporter leur contenu avant cette échéance. Microsoft précise que ce chantier n'en est qu'à ses débuts, avec davantage de détails partagés dans les prochains mois..
- Intégration de DALL-E 3 pour une création d'images plus créatives et réalistes
- Capacité de traitement des images par GPT-4 Vision pour des réponses contextuelles précises
- Interface conviviale et intégrée dans divers produits Microsoft

articles.title: ETH Zurich spin-off Aisot Technologies bags €2.13 million to bring agentic AI to portfolio management | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Aisot Technologies (Aisot), a Zurich-based startup offering AI-driven portfolio intelligence for institutional investors, has closed a €2.13 million (CHF 2 million) Seed extension round.
The round was backed by existing and new investors, including family offices and experienced angel investors. Also joining as a new investor is Felix Haldner, former Partner at Partners Group and former President of the Swiss Funds & Asset Management Association (SFAMA).
“The fact that our existing investors continue to expand their trust, while we’ve also gained experienced figures like Felix Haldner as new supporters, confirms we’re on the right path. We want to help wealth managers in Switzerland and internationally to integrate AI into their investment processes in a way that is well-founded, transparent and impactful,” said Stefan Klauser, co-founder and CEO of Aisot Technologies.
Founded in 2021 as an official ETH Zurich spin-off, Aisot offers AI-driven solutions for portfolio optimisation and risk management to asset and wealth managers and family offices.
The company states that it combines quantitative financial analysis, machine learning and LLM-based news sentiment analysis into institutionally deployable forecasting and decision-making models.
The platform helps large asset managers identify additional signals and gives smaller investment firms access to professional data, AI and quant infrastructure for portfolio construction and personalisation, without having to build and operate it themselves.
The company highlights that its agentic AI delivers data-driven decision support across the full portfolio management lifecycle, from strategy and backtesting to rebalancing, optimisation, and monitoring.
“We are convinced that Aisot’s solutions can generate significant efficiency gains for asset and wealth managers, including in analysis, portfolio management and product development. Aisot Technologies’ models also deliver signals across different investment strategies, with the aim of contributing to return optimisation,” said Felix Haldner.
In March 2023, the company announced that it had secured €1.91 million (CHF 1.8 million) in a Seed funding round led by Haute Capital Partners. In March 2021, Aisot closed a pre-Seed round of €246.9k ($285k) led by F10, a Zurich-based startup incubator and accelerator, and complemented by family and friends investors,
The company has a network of partners and employees across Europe, Asia and the US. The team consists of experienced experts in artificial intelligence, natural language processing and financial mathematics.

articles.title: KI besteht Onlinekurse statt Studierender – Hochschulen suchen Antworten
articles.text:
Mit KI-Agenten schummeln: Wie Studierende die Tools komplette Onlinekurse absolvieren lassen
Künstliche Intelligenz ist vielen Lehrkräften schon seit Monaten ein Dorn im Auge. Sie beklagen, dass zahlreiche Studierende und Schüler:innen zu den KI-Tools greifen, um Hausaufgaben zu erledigen und Aufsätze schreiben zu lassen. Ein Professor erwischte seine Studierenden erst kürzlich per Prompt-Injektion bei der KI-Nutzung, während in Mexiko 60.000 Studierende eine Aufnahmeprüfung wiederholen müssen, weil sie mit den Tools online geschummelt haben.
KI-Agenten übernehmen Blackboard und Canvas
Gerade für asynchrones Lernen mit Onlinekursen ist KI zu einem Störfaktor geworden. Die New York Times hat dafür mehrere Lehrkräfte interviewt, die digitale Kurse und Prüfungen für ihre Studierenden anbieten. Laut ihnen sind einige ihrer Student:innen mittlerweile dazu übergegangen, KI-Agenten statt Chatbots einzusetzen, um Onlinekurse zu bestehen. Sie befehlen den Tools „Logge dich ein und absolviere das Quiz“, um Prüfungen zu bestehen.
Da KI-Agenten sich über Konnektoren mit Diensten wie Canvas, Brightspace und Blackboard verbinden können, sind diese Aufgaben mittlerweile keine große Herausforderung mehr. Die Agenten loggen sich bei den Diensten ein, analysieren die bereitgestellten Lernmaterialien und füllen dann die Multiple-Choice-Tests oder interagieren laut den Lehrkräften sogar mit anderen Studierenden per Chat.
Ein wirksames Mittel, um die KI-Agenten von den Onlineplattformen auszusperren, wurde bisher nicht gefunden. Zwar gibt es Indikatoren, wie die Zeit, die zur Bearbeitung von Aufgaben gebraucht wurde, doch kann die KI-Nutzung damit nicht hundertprozentig bewiesen werden. Jason Weaver, Chief of Staff bei Blackboard, sagte dazu: „Unsere Kund:innen machen es sehr deutlich, dass es noch nie zuvor einen solch enormen Druck auf die akademische Integrität gab.“ Blackboard hat zur KI-Abwehr ein Unternehmen aufgekauft, dessen App den Rhythmus beim Tippen von Texten analysieren soll, um Nutzer:innen als echte Menschen auszuweisen.
Tipp-Rhythmus und Präsenztests als Antwort auf KI-Betrug
Da KI-Detektoren aber auch keine hundertprozentige Genauigkeit bieten, müssen sich Lehrkräfte andere Mittel und Wege einfallen lassen, um die Agenten aus den digitalen Klassenzimmern fernzuhalten. Einige der Professor:innen sind dazu übergegangen, ihre Tests persönlicher zu gestalten. Statt einfach nur einen Multiple-Choice-Bogen auszufüllen, müssen Studierende ihre eigene Meinung zu Themen formulieren. Kathryn Kysar, Professorin für Community Colleges, sagt dazu: „Diejenigen von uns, die seit sehr langer Zeit lehren und selbst Redakteur:innen und Schreiber:innen sind, können billig produzierten KI-Kram innerhalb von 30 Sekunden erkennen.“
Einige Lehrkräfte wählen einen anderen Ansatz und verlagern das digitale Klassenzimmer wieder mehr in die echte Welt. Marina Aminy, Executive Director des California Virtual Campus, rät etwa dazu, statt Onlineprüfungen flexible Präsenztests anzubieten. Diese finden dann zu mehreren Zeiten an verschiedenen Tagen statt, um Studierenden mehr Auswahl für den Zeitpunkt des Absolvierens zu geben.
Jordan Canzonetta und das Vertrauen in eigene Schreibfähigkeiten
Wieder andere Professor:innen regen ihre Schüler:innen dazu an, über den Einsatz von KI genauer nachzudenken. Sie sollen merken, dass sie die Agenten und Chatbots nicht benötigen, um gute Texte zu formulieren. Jordan Canzonetta, Professor an der Lewis-Universität, sagt: „Meine größte Herausforderung dabei ist es, die Studierenden dazu zu bringen, in ihre Schreibfertigkeiten zu vertrauen. Und darin, dass sie etwas Wichtiges mitzuteilen haben.“

articles.title: Max severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw now targeted in attacks
articles.text:
A maximum-severity SAP Commerce Cloud remote code execution vulnerability patched three days ago is already being targeted in attacks, according to threat intelligence company Defused.
Commerce Cloud (formerly known as SAP Hybris) is a cloud-based e-commerce platform used by online stores owned by high-profile global brands and large retailers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-58231, this critical flaw stems from an improper authorization weakness in the core Data Hub Adapter extension for Commerce Cloud that threat actors without privileges can exploit in low-complexity attacks to execute arbitrary code.
"SAP Commerce Cloud allows an unauthenticated attacker to abuse a default authentication client and submit specially crafted input to certain functions lacking sufficient validation," SAP explains.
"Successful exploitation could enable arbitrary code execution and compromise internal components, resulting in high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the application."
While SAP has yet to flag this security flaw as actively exploited in a security advisory issued this Tuesday, Defused security researchers confirmed earlier today that CVE-2026-58231 is now being targeted in the wild.
"First exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-58231 (unauth RCE in SAP Commerce Cloud, CVSS 10.0) is now hitting our honeypots - 3 days after patch day," Defused warned in a Friday tweet. "This vulnerability has no public PoC and is not known to be exploited."
A SAP spokesperson told BleepingComputer that the company is aware of and investigating this issue when asked to confirm Defused's report.
"A security note https://me.sap.com/notes/3771065 is published and available for SAP customers and partners and was released on SAP’s August Patch Day. We recommend customers and partners patch their systems with immediate effect," the spokesperson added.
Internet security watchdog group Shadowserver tracks over 4,200 IP addresses with a SAP Commerce Cloud fingerprint, most of them from Europe and North America.
However, there is no information on how many of them are honeypots or have already been secured against CVE-2026-58231 attacks.
Most recently, SAP fixed 16 vulnerabilities in its July 2026 Security Patch package and 30 more vulnerabilities in June and May, including three more critical security flaws (CVE-2026-44761, CVE-2026-22732, and CVE-2026-34263) affecting the Commerce Cloud enterprise-grade e-commerce platform.
In April, cybersecurity companies Aikido and Socket also reported that attackers aiming to steal credentials from developers' systems compromised multiple official SAP npm packages in a supply chain attack.
Since November 2021, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added 14 SAP vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including three that were abused in ransomware attacks.
SAP is a German multinational software corporation that serves 99 of the 100 largest companies worldwide and has reported total revenues exceeding €36 billion in fiscal year 2025.

articles.title: Un iPhone dans les mains d'un bébé : Apple fait scandale avec sa nouvelle pub
articles.text:
Tout part d’un panneau publicitaire milanais et du signalement d’une habitante de la ville. Le 7 août, l’AGIA, l’autorité italienne garante de l’enfance et de l’adolescence, a annoncé avoir transmis le dossier à trois instances à la fois. Sont concernés le régulateur des communications, l’autorité de la concurrence et l’organisme d’autodiscipline publicitaire. En cause, une déclinaison locale de la campagne mondiale d’Apple vantant la sérénité iPhone, où un tout-petit manipule le smartphone sous un slogan qui se veut rassurant : « Tutto ok, è iPhone » (tout va bien, c’est un iPhone).
La pub qui fait passer l’iPhone pour un babysitter
La campagne montre d’ordinaire des iPhone survivant aux accidents du quotidien, la pluie, le coup de patte d’un chat, la gueule d’un chien ; le bambin joue vraisemblablement le rôle du crash test suivant. L’autorité y a lu tout autre chose et dénonce la « normalisation du baby-sitting électronique », formule qui donne son titre au communiqué. Le reproche ne porte donc ni sur un produit défectueux ni sur une allégation mensongère, mais sur le message lui-même. Montrer un bambin captivé par un écran dans une publicité grand format, c’est présenter comme normale (et même apaisante, tout va bien puisque c’est un iPhone) une pratique que les pédiatres passent leurs journées à décourager. L’affaire a suffisamment ému pour déclencher une triple saisine, un traitement d’ordinaire réservé aux dossiers sensibles. Elle intervient de surcroît dans un pays où le débat sur les écrans et les mineurs occupe déjà le terrain politique.
Lire aussi : Votre enfant passe 10 fois plus de temps sur son smartphone qu’à lire : ce que ça fait à son cerveau
La suite appartient aux trois instances saisies, qui peuvent aussi bien classer l’affaire qu’exiger le retrait de la campagne, voire sanctionner. Apple n’a pas commenté publiquement à ce stade. La firme connaît pourtant la maison : l’autorité italienne de la concurrence lui avait infligé en 2020 une amende de 10 millions d’euros pour ses promesses exagérées sur la résistance à l’eau des iPhone. L’Italie n’est pas le terrain de jeu le plus indulgent d’Europe pour la firme.
Apple peut-il encore jouer les moralisateurs des écrans ?
Le plus piquant du dossier tient à l’identité de l’accusé. Apple est l’entreprise qui a généralisé Temps d’écran pour surveiller nos usages, puis la fonction Distance d’écran, censée protéger les yeux des plus jeunes en les avertissant quand l’iPhone est trop près du visage. La firme qui vous facture la vertu numérique en option de série se retrouve à afficher en 4 par 3 l’exact comportement que ses propres outils prétendent combattre. Vendre le poison et l’antidote dans la même boîte, il fallait un certain aplomb marketing.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que la marque ajuste sa communication sous pression locale, et l’issue italienne dira si le panneau survit à l’été. Côté français, en revanche, les repères sanitaires n’ont rien d’ambigu : les autorités de santé recommandent zéro écran avant 3 ans, iPhone compris, aussi rassurant soit le slogan. Les parents qui doutaient trouveront dans cette affaire un rappel utile, offert malgré elle par Apple.

articles.title: Terremotos atingem Indonésia e Espanha nesta sexta-feira (14)
articles.text:
Um forte terremoto de magnitude 7,7 atingiu a costa da Indonésia nesta sexta-feira (14), segundo o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS). O epicentro foi localizado próximo à ilha de Flores, na província de Nusa Tenggara Oriental, região conhecida pela intensa atividade sísmica. Há relato de pelo menos duas mortes.
O tremor ocorreu às 5h58 de sábado (15) no horário local (18h58 de sexta-feira [14] no horário de Brasília). O epicentro ficou a aproximadamente 68 quilômetros ao norte-noroeste de Ende, cidade localizada na ilha de Flores. O USGS estimou a profundidade em apenas dez quilômetros, característica que pode aumentar o potencial de impactos na superfície.
As informações sobre a magnitude passaram por revisões ao longo das primeiras horas após o terremoto. A versão inicial divulgada por alguns centros de monitoramento apontava valores menores, mas o USGS posteriormente registrou o evento como magnitude 7,7. A localização e a profundidade também apresentaram pequenas diferenças entre os órgãos sismológicos.
Alerta de tsunami
- Após o terremoto, a Agência de Meteorologia, Climatologia e Geofísica da Indonésia (BMKG) emitiu alerta de tsunami para áreas costeiras potencialmente afetadas;
- As autoridades orientaram moradores a se afastarem de praias e margens de rios e procurarem terrenos mais elevados enquanto o risco fosse avaliado. A recomendação ocorreu porque terremotos fortes e rasos próximos ao litoral podem deslocar grandes volumes de água e provocar ondas potencialmente perigosas;
- O alerta abrangia áreas da província de Nusa Tenggara Oriental e outras regiões que poderiam sofrer efeitos do tsunami. Autoridades passaram a acompanhar os níveis do mar por meio de estações de monitoramento para determinar se ondas significativas seriam registradas;
- Até as primeiras informações divulgadas após o tremor, não havia confirmação imediata de mortes ou grandes danos materiais.
Leia mais:
- Como funciona e como usar o alerta de terremotos no celular Android
- Saiba onde estão acontecendo todos os terremotos no mundo
- O que é um terremoto subaquático e qual sua relação com um tsunami?
Região é altamente sujeita a terremotos
A Indonésia está localizada no chamado Círculo de Fogo do Pacífico, área de intensa atividade tectônica que concentra grande parte dos terremotos e vulcões do planeta.
O arquipélago indonésio possui mais de 17 mil ilhas e está situado em região onde diferentes placas tectônicas se encontram. A ilha de Flores e seus arredores estão entre as áreas do país frequentemente afetadas por terremotos.
O forte tremor desta sexta ocorreu em região próxima ao encontro das placas Australiana e de Sunda, configuração geológica que contribui para a elevada atividade sísmica local.
A profundidade relativamente pequena do terremoto aumenta a preocupação das autoridades, pois eventos rasos tendem a produzir movimentos mais intensos na superfície quando comparados a terremotos de magnitude semelhante que ocorrem em grandes profundidades.
Tremores secundários
Após o terremoto principal, outros tremores foram registrados na região. A ocorrência de réplicas é comum depois de terremotos de grande magnitude e pode representar risco adicional para estruturas que tenham sido danificadas pelo primeiro evento.
As autoridades indonésias mantêm o monitoramento da região justamente para acompanhar possíveis novos tremores e eventuais alterações no nível do mar.
A situação ainda estava em avaliação nas primeiras horas após o terremoto, e os dados sobre magnitude, profundidade, danos e risco de tsunami poderiam sofrer novas atualizações conforme os órgãos responsáveis analisarem os registros do evento.
Terremoto de magnitude 3,7 é registrado na Espanha
Um terremoto de magnitude 3,7 foi registrado nesta sexta-feira (14) na região de La Zubia, na província de Granada, no sul da Espanha. O tremor ocorreu às 18h43 no horário local (13h43 no horário de Brasília) e foi sentido em diferentes municípios da província e também na região da Costa Tropical.
Outro tremor, de magnitude 2,9, foi registrado pouco antes, às 18h11, no mar de Alborão, próximo à costa espanhola. Registros sísmicos apontam ainda a ocorrência de outros abalos de baixa magnitude na Espanha e em áreas próximas ao longo desta sexta.
Apesar de terem ocorrido no mesmo dia, não há indicação de que os tremores registrados na Espanha tenham relação com o terremoto de magnitude 7,7 que atingiu a Indonésia. O evento indonésio teve epicentro próximo à ilha de Flores, a milhares de quilômetros de distância da Península Ibérica.
Os dois fenômenos são, portanto, tratados como eventos sísmicos independentes. Até o momento, não há informações de danos significativos associados ao tremor registrado na província de Granada.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Alerte rouge sur l'iPhone : Apple prévient des centaines d'utilisateurs d'une opération espionnage
articles.text:
Apple vient à nouveau de mettre en garde les utilisateurs d’iPhone, d’iPad et de Mac. Le géant de Cupertino indique avoir déployé une nouvelle salve de notifications concernant un logiciel espion sur les appareils d’utilisateurs répartis dans 110 pays. Les appareils concernés pourraient avoir été compromis par un spyware habituellement utilisé par des gouvernements. L’alerte a d’abord été repérée par John Scott-Railton, chercheur principal chez Citizen Lab.
 ALERT: Did you get a notification like this today?
Seek expert security help asap!
Apple just sent out a fresh round of threat notifications about mercenary spyware.
That means tech like Pegasus used by governments to spy on you.
Here are steps to take right now 1/ pic.twitter.com/KFnZW3itFJ
— John Scott-Railton (@jsrailton) August 13, 2026
Ces alertes, désormais diffusées directement sur l’écran verrouillé d’iOS, indiquent qu’Apple a « détecté une attaque de logiciel espion mercenaire visant votre iPhone » et que « des mesures existent pour protéger vos données et votre appareil dès maintenant ». Comme toujours, Apple n’a pas précisé le nombre exact de personnes averties ni les pays spécifiquement visés par la cyberattaque.
A lire aussi : Apple corrige une faille critique du partage d’écran du Mac, installez la mise à jour
Un dispositif d’alerte né en 2021
Ce n’est pas la première fois qu’Apple recourt à ce type d’alerte. Le système d’alerte sur l’iPhone existe en fait depuis 2021. Interrogé par TechCrunch, le groupe américain précise que le dispositif a permis d’avertir des clients dans plus de 150 pays à ce jour. Le système d’avertissement a été mis en place dans le sillage du scandale Pegasus. Il a notamment été utilisé pour alerter des utilisateurs en France en février dernier.
Dans un nouvel article d’assistance publié sur son site web, Apple explique avoir revu le fonctionnement du dispositif d’alerte pour améliorer son efficacité. Dorénavant, l’alerte s’affiche directement sur l’écran de l’iPhone, même si celui-ci est verrouillé. Outre la notification sur l’écran verrouillé, l’entreprise envoie également un e-mail. Par ailleurs, Apple affiche systématiquement l’alerte lorsque l’utilisateur se connecte à son compte Apple.
« Les notifications de menaces d’Apple fournissent des informations complémentaires et des recommandations pour protéger vos comptes et appareils », explique Apple sur son site, mettant notamment en avant le mode Isolement (Lockdown Mode) sur iPhone.
Ce mode blinde votre smartphone contre les cyberattaques sophistiquées en limitant les fonctionnalités qui peuvent servir comme porte d’entrée. Selon la firme, aucun cas de compromission confirmée n’a été recensé sur un appareil où ce mode était activé.
Des attaques « plus sophistiquées que les cyberattaques classiques »
L’avertissement ne signifie pas automatiquement que l’iPhone a été piraté. Apple précise bien qu’il s’agit d’un simple signal indiquant qu’une activité suspecte a été repérée. Celle-ci laisse penser que l’utilisateur a été spécifiquement visé par un virus espion, vraisemblablement déployé par des pirates mandatés par des gouvernements.
« Ces attaques sont bien plus sophistiquées que les cyberattaques classiques, car les auteurs de ces attaques déploient des ressources considérables pour cibler un nombre très restreint d’individus et leurs appareils. Les attaques de logiciels espions mercenaires coûtent des millions de dollars et ont souvent une durée de vie très courte, ce qui les rend beaucoup plus difficiles à détecter et à prévenir », souligne Apple.
Dans la plupart des cas, les cibles sont des journalistes, des dissidents politiques, des militants, des hommes politiques, ou des hauts fonctionnaires. Les attaques ne concernent généralement pas des utilisateurs lambda.

articles.title: Shell investigates 'potential incident' after Clop data theft claims
articles.text:
Oil giant Shell has confirmed it is investigating a potential security incident after the Clop ransomware gang claimed it stole 89GB of data.
Shell is a British multinational energy conglomerate and one of the world's top three oil and gas companies, after Chevron and ExxonMobil. It has 85,000 employees in more than 70 countries and operates a massive network of tens of thousands of service and recharge stations that serve over 20 million customers daily.
According to a recent post on Clop's dark web data leak site, the allegedly stolen files include engineering drawings, scans of facility testing reports, photos of the facilities, and project plans.
"We are aware of a potential incident. We are working with our security teams and relevant experts to investigate," a Shell spokesperson told BleepingComputer when asked to confirm Clop's data theft claims.
While the company has yet to share more information, the Clop gang listed it on its leak site as one of 43 new victims likely targeted in data theft attacks against Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM instances exploiting a critical improper input validation vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-12569.
As part of the same attacks, Clop also claimed it stole sensitive data, including backups, system files, projects, drawings, diagrams, and blueprints, from the networks of tech conglomerates General Electric and Philips.
GE and Philips spokespersons were not immediately available for comment when BleepingComputer contacted them earlier today. A PTC spokesperson has also yet to reply to a request for comment.
PTC began releasing CVE-2026-12569 security patches on June 17 and, even though it didn't confirm in-the-wild exploitation, it also released a private advisory urging customers to review environments for indicators of compromise (IOCs).
After PTC warned customers of "heightened threat activity" on June 26, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also confirmed that the flaw is actively exploited in attacks, adding it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and ordering federal agencies to secure their PTC Windchill and FlexPLM instances within three days.
CVE-2026-12569 also prompted emergency action from German authorities, with the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) warning PTC customers in the middle of the night to patch their systems as quickly as possible.
Clop's Windchill and FlexPLM attacks were also confirmed by the Ransomware Information Sharing and Analysis Centre (Ransom-ISAC), a non-profit organization dedicated to the tracking and defense against ransomware threats, and by cybersecurity company ReliaQuest, which said that the threat actors have been deploying JSP webshells that allow them to steal sensitive data from victims' compromised PLM platforms.
PTC FlexPLM and PTC Windchill are enterprise software platforms in the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) category, used to track, design, and manage products up to final manufacturing.
The two systems are widely popular among engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams at high-profile companies across the aerospace, defense, automotive, heavy machinery, retail, and medtech sectors. PTC says that its products are used by over 30,000 customers globally, including more than 1,500 brand and retail customers using FlexPLM.

articles.title: Le PDG de Saber Interactive confirme l'usage de l'IA pour les dialogues de Rideshare Stimulator après les accusations d'une ancienne scénariste
articles.text:
Il était une fois, le 11 août 2026 précisément, une employée de Saber Interactive qui en avait gros. Stella Sacco, scénariste principale du jeu Rideshare « Stimulator », édité par Saber, sur lequel elle a travaillé avec le développeur Unigine, a révélé que le jeu avait été conçu à l’aide d’IA générative et qu’elle avait tout bonnement été remplacée par ChatGPT.
« J’étais la scénariste principale sur ce projet ! Et Saber m’a remplacée par ChatGPT en cours de développement. Toutes les voix des passagers étaient aussi générées par IA. Soit ils ont changé d’orientation à un moment donné, soit ils ne le précisent pas sur Steam », a écrit Stella Sacco sur Bluesky.
À la lecture du message, Matthew Karch, le cofondateur et PDG de Saber Interactive, a vu rouge : « Stella qui ? J’ai dû poser la question à Claude, car je ne lui ai jamais parlé et je ne l’ai jamais vue. Nous avons déjà annoncé que nous utiliserions l’IA pour certains aspects du jeu et nous mettrons à jour la page Steam une fois les fonctionnalités finalisées », a-t-il répondu dans un communiqué publié le 13 août sur le site This Week in Video Games.
Une réponse d’une agressivité rare, qui montre surtout que l’utilisation de l’IA dans le développement de Rideshare « Stimulator » n’est visiblement pas un secret. Si Matthew Karch affirme que, dans l’éventualité où le scénario du jeu remporterait un prix, celui-ci serait remis à une personne capable de monter sur scène pour le recevoir — comprendre : pas une IA –, il explique néanmoins avoir prévu de préciser plus tard l’utilisation de l’IA dans le développement du jeu. Il indique : « Nous considérons l’utilisation de l’IA dans ce jeu — qui sera proposé à un prix réduit — comme un avantage pour les consommateurs », a-t-il déclaré. « Stella a rompu sa clause de confidentialité et a vendu la mèche avant que nous ne soyons prêts. »
L’IA a bel et bien été utilisée pour des dialogues dans le jeu
« Quant à Stella, elle a été remplacée par une personne plus talentueuse, puis licenciée pour diverses raisons quelques mois plus tard. À en juger par ce que je vois, elle aime la controverse encore plus que moi. Avec le recul, j’aurais franchement préféré la remplacer par une IA. Au moins, nous aurions eu affaire à quelqu’un programmé pour être honnête », enchérit le PDG de Saber Interactive, qui veut décidément avoir le dernier mot.
Stella Sacco a répondu sur Bluesky : « Je pense qu’il devrait être évident pour quiconque lit cette déclaration qu’il réagit avec agressivité parce qu’il ne voulait pas que l’on sache que de l’IA avait été utilisée dans le jeu […]. Cette déclaration est remarquablement pathétique pour un PDG ; couplée à l’utilisation de l’IA, elle nuira bien davantage à la réputation de Saber qu’à la mienne. »
Rideshare « Stimulator », prévu cette année sur PC, Xbox Series X/S et PS5, est un jeu de gestion de taxi dans lequel les passagers ont des histoires imprévisibles à raconter. Au final, le jeu s’est vu apposer le tag « Artificial Intelligence » sur sa page Steam.
Selon les informations dévoilées par Saber, via Gamefile, les dialogues sont générés à partir de prompts rédigés par des scénaristes, puis vérifiés, tandis que la narration est intégralement écrite par des humains : « Ce sont des humains qui ont écrit l’histoire, dans son intégralité. Je veux dire, ce n’est pas de la prose digne de Shakespeare, mais c’est mieux que ce que Claude aurait pu produire. Cela dit, à en croire ce que me dit mon équipe, cette remarque ne s’applique peut-être pas à l’auteur en question », conclut Matthew Karch, toujours dans la bienveillance.

articles.title: Mantener un cajero en la Antártida es una pesadilla logística. La solución es canibalizar otro
articles.text:
Con el auge del dinero digital, y de los pagos móviles, somos muchos los que salimos a la calle sin la cartera. En mi caso, creo que paso menos por el cajero que por la peluquería, el efectivo hace tiempo que me parece prescindible. Pero ¿y si necesito unos billetes? No suele haber mucho problema, todo depende de lo aislado que esté el lugar. Por eso me extrañó que en la Antártida haya cajeros.
Espera. ¿Cajeros en la Antártida? Pues sí. Y no es en singular, que hay dos, uno al lado del otro. Son del banco estadounidense Wells Fargo, tienen un récord Guinness por ser los cajeros que se encuentran más al sur del mundo y están localizados en la base científica McMurdo que Estados Unidos tiene en la Antártida.
La historia. La base McMurdo (McMurdo Station) conforma un asentamiento científico que comenzó su construcción el 18 de diciembre de 1955 para abrir oficialmente en 1956. Está situada en las coordenadas 77° 50.89’ S y 166° 40.11’ E, la infraestructura consta de 146 edificios y en ellos no solo se albergan las instalaciones científicas, también distintos servicios para quienes habitan la base: unas 1.100 personas a la semana en verano y unas 200 en invierno.
La base acumula una gran rotación de científicos y personal dedicado al mantenimiento. Por ello, en McMurdo hay una tienda, una cafetería, el Gallagher's Pub y hasta un festival de música que se celebra en verano: el Icestock, el festival más austral del mundo. Con esta perspectiva, me parece menos extraño que haya cajeros en la Antártida.
Los problemas. Wells Fargo instaló sus dos cajeros de McMurdo en 1998. Uno está al lado del otro, como si el banco esperase largas colas para sacar dinero y operar con las cuentas. Pero no: solo uno es el que funciona, suelen hacerlo de manera alterna. Por una razón: para no quedarse sin ambos a la vez.
Como explicó Kristopher Dahl, un representante de Wells Fargo, a Mental Floss:
“Cada dos años, se revisan ambas máquinas y se ponen al día con los últimos avances tecnológicos”
Kristopher Dahl señaló que Wells Fargo entrena al personal de la base para que reparen los cajeros en caso de necesidad, al menos mientras sean reparaciones básicas. De necesitarlo, uno de los cajeros es “canibalizado” para extraerle las piezas para el otro. No solo eso: son los propios empleados de la tienda los que recargan con billetes las máquinas.
Dinero circular. En la Antártida no hay muchos sitios donde gastar el dinero. Así que el efectivo circula entre los pocos negocios que hay en la base. Dado que los billetes se acabarían pronto si la fuente que los surte se agota, los propios comercios recargan los cajeros. Es un Juan Palomo en toda regla.
La paradoja. Mientras una base de la Antártida tiene dos cajeros para dar servicio a apenas mil personas, con suerte y en verano, en España el parque no deja de encoger: había 41.842 cajeros al final de 2024, 1.230 menos solo con respecto a 2023, según el Banco de España. Oficinas que cierran, máquinas que se desmontan y ciudadanos de pueblos apartados cuya única opción de acceder a un cajero es desplazarse decenas de kilómetros en coche.
Seguiré sin apenas visitar los cajeros, pero me quedo con la lección que deja la base de McMurdo: el efectivo que llevas encima es lo único que aguanta cuando todos los sistemas fallan. Es algo que ya experimentamos durante el repentino apagón que sufrimos en 2025. Y supone un claro aviso para los sistemas que están por llegar, como el euro digital.

articles.title: Over 1,000 Charities Hit by Beacon CRM Data Breach
articles.text:
UK-based customer relationship management (CRM) provider Beacon revealed this week the likely root cause of a recent data breach affecting many organizations.
Beacon’s CRM platform is designed for charities and other non-profit organizations to manage donors, supporters, volunteers, and related fundraising and service activities.
The company revealed in early August that it had suffered a data breach in which hackers downloaded customer database backups. The data was encrypted, but Beacon admitted that the attackers could have decrypted it prior to exfiltration.
In an update shared this week, Beacon reported that the earliest malicious activity was observed on July 27 and the hackers likely transferred the data on July 27-28.
“Specific objects, exact destination of the downloads, and definitive attribution of which objects were accessed cannot be determined from available logs,” the company noted. “However, having reviewed the data transfer volume and the total volume of data stored across the system, our assessment is that the threat actor exported all data contained within the database.”
Beacon’s investigation found that the threat actor obtained the data from an AWS environment by using a compromised AWS access key that may have been exposed in publicly available JavaScript build artifacts.
Several of the affected UK charities have issued their own statements on the matter, with some revealing that the incident affects all of Beacon’s more than 1,000 customers.
Some charities said personal information belonging to supporters may have been compromised, including names, phone numbers, email addresses, and postal addresses.
Others pointed out that no bank account numbers, sort codes, card numbers, or card security details have been exposed, as they do not store such sensitive financial information.
The UK government’s Charity Commission is monitoring the situation and has issued guidance for affected organizations.
No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for the attack on Beacon. The company says it’s not aware of the stolen data being published.

articles.title: I used Claude AI to build a Breakout clone in five minutes — and you can play it
articles.text:
A year ago, it took Claude AI and me hours to build Asteroids; we just built a Breakout clone in five minutes — and you can play it
AI development is really breaking out
I didn't set out to build a Breakout clone, but that's what I — or really Claude, under my direction — did, and it took less time than it takes to watch a half dozen cat videos.
Here's how it started. Claude was having issues. Anthropic's powerful and popular generative AI platform was apparently going up and down, and some were complaining, but when I checked, Claude told me, "I'm doing well, thanks for asking!" I realized, though, that if the problems were intermittent, I might need a tougher task to test Claude's overall stability.
More than a year ago, I worked with Claude, or rather guided Claude through the process of recreating the early 1980s arcade game classic: Asteroids. The final game, which Claude exported as a shareable artifact, was the product of hours of guidance and back-and-forth between me and the AI. It didn't start off great, but with each prompt, we iterated, and the game improved until I had a rather robust and true-to-the-original Asteroids knockoff.
With that in mind, I tasked Claude AI, running the free Sonnet 5 model at "Medium" level, with creating a Breakout clone.
Breaking out
Breakout is one of my favorite games, something I've played on early consoles, PCs, and even my old BlackBerry, where "Brick Breaker" was one of the few preloaded games.
The game rules are pretty simple. There's a multi-level brick wall (usually eight bricks deep) at the top of the screen, a paddle at the base, and a bouncing ball you bounce off the paddle to break down the brick wall.
For my prompt, I tried to describe, in some detail, my game, and was not coy about it being an online version of Breakout:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Let's make a quick game. I want an online version of the old Breakout game, but let's replace the bricks with robots that are always slowly marching down toward you (if they reach you, it's game over). The ball that you bounce off your side-sliding controller is a gear that breaks up the robots easily in the first level. In the second level, the robots are shinier and harder, and the gear takes three or more hits to break and make a robot disappear. If you clear the level, the gear turns into a titanium ball that bounces faster but is more powerful. Controls are either keyboard/arrow based and mouseable. Want this to result in a web-based, shareable game, so a link/artifact I can share online.
That's all the direction I gave it. I didn't describe colors, the initial speed of the ball, or even how quickly the robots would march down the screen. I didn't get into details about the look of the robots, instead relying on generalities and some material descriptions to help guide Claude.
It took me a minute or two to write the prompt and around three minutes for Claude to deliver the results, which it cleverly called "Gearbreaker".
I got a brief description of gameplay and levels (there are just two for now) :
"How it plays:
Level 1 — matte robots, one hit each from the spinning gear ball. They march downward on a timer; let them cross the dashed red hazard line and it's instant game over.
Level 2 — shinier robots (metallic gradient, cyan eyes) that soak up 3 hits, shown as pips along the bottom of each unit. Same gear ball, tougher targets.
Clear level 2 → the ball forges into a titanium core: bigger, faster, hits for 2 damage instead of 1. Levels keep scaling procedurally after that (more rows, faster march, tougher units), so it runs endless with a local high-score save.
Controls: arrow keys or mouse to slide the paddle, Space or click to launch/pause/restart. Basic touch support too."
On the right side of the screen, there was my playable game. There's also the artifact publish button, which I chose to use so I could share the game with you.
It's a stunningly complete render of a completely playable and, in some ways, challenging Breakout clone, and it took five minutes. I'd call the design clean and efficient. The bricks have a robot look, and the ball is a blue spinning gear (in the first level). The movement and physics are basically perfect, and there's enough on-screen instruction to easily grasp gameplay.
Just the beginning
It's just another mind-boggling example of the incredible pace of AI development. While I had expected a playable game, I assumed it would be missing enough crucial components to make it dull or uninteresting — something similar to my earlier AI game development projects. Instead, I got something that displays a clear understanding of the purpose of such a game: challenge, entertainment, and replayability.
Using my mouse, I played through a couple of times, failing to break all the bricks in Level One and ending the game. I realized I had to take Claude's output more seriously, and, with some effort, as I watched the robot bricks steadily march down my screen, I finally cleared all the bricks in Level One and then started in on the tougher Level Two. As I had instructed, the robots on the second level looked and reacted differently. It now took at least three direct hits to make them disappear. I failed and already want to play again.
This is by no means the wildest example of the AI development process or vibe coding; it's just me prompting Claude to code a complete game with the barest of instructions.
Claude and these models cannot do this on their own, but it does make you think about the agentic AI that's now being unleashed on the world. It's more powerful and autonomous. I could imagine someone asking one to start work on recreating all the popular video games of the last half century. The only limit would be time and compute tokens.
Speaking of which, Claude just informed me that this Breakout task used up about 90% of my credits for the day. I think it was worth it.
Take the game for a spin and let me know what you think in the comments below.

articles.title: Can Canada function without American tech? | BetaKit
articles.text:
What would happen if, overnight, Canada suddenly lost all access to American tech?
That question was posed by our friends at the Canadian Shield Institute, who have put together an infographic outlining what the average day might look like without the economic and technological integration Canadians have come to expect—maybe even depend on.
“When we talk about sovereignty, we’re talking about strategic capacity. Can you govern yourself with the tools that you have?”
You can play with the infographic yourself, but the TL;DR is not great: while there are some viable Canadian alternatives, our country just doesn’t have a complete ‘sovereign tech stack.’ It’s part of the reason why our 2026 BetaKit Most Ambitious issue, which tells stories of Canadian innovators strengthening our security, autonomy, and prosperity, has an entire section dedicated to the companies trying to fill those gaps.
In that section, we also have an op-ed from Canadian Shield Institute managing director, Vass Bednar, asking another important question: how sovereign is sovereign enough? Do we really need a Canadian version of every app or service or technology, or is there a better way?
This week on the podcast, Vass joins to answer that question and a whole bunch of others, like what does minimum viable sovereignty for Canadian tech look like? How should we evaluate recent ‘elbows up’ federal policy initiatives? And maybe the biggest question of all: what does sovereignty really mean for Canadians in an ever more interconnected digital world?
Subscribe: Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts, RSS
The answers might be as tough to parse as the questions, but Vass is an apex-level policy wonk and has an incredible way of explaining complex subjects so that Canadians can engage with them.
So let’s do that! Let’s engage. Let’s… dig in.

Amid global uncertainty, the path forward is clear: Canada’s moment to build is now.

articles.title: Lo próximo de WhatsApp son fondos animados en los chats y una mayor personalización, pero no te emociones
articles.text:
WhatsApp sigue buscando nuevas funcionalidades para ofrecerles a sus usuarios mayor personalización. Y aunque las opciones que ofrece la compañía a este sentido son bastante limitadas comparadas con la competencia, lo cierto es que ha ido añadiendo funcionalidades conforme ha pasado el tiempo. Pero no lo suficiente, y WhatsApp lo sabe.
Por ello, la compañía está trabajando en dos nuevas funcionalidades para ofrecer mayor personalización a los chats y a la propia aplicación. Entre ellas, hay una función muy esperada por los usuarios, y que desde luego añadirá una capa enorme de personalización: los fondos de pantalla de chats animados.
Según explican en WABetaInfo, la última versión de WhatsApp para iOS disponible en TestFlight incluye referencias a algo que ya se había encontrado en una beta reciente para Android, pero del que no había nuevas noticias: nuevos conjuntos de temas para chats llamados Destacado, Doodle y Minimalista.
La clave aquí está en que se trata, por primera vez, de fondos de pantalla totalmente dinámicos. En este sentido, Minimalista utilizará fondos de color blanco o negro sólido, dependiendo de si está activado el modo claro u oscuro; hasta ahí todo normal. La clave está en la opción Destacados, que por primera vez incluirá fondos de pantalla con un movimiento sutil, es decir, animados.
Fondos animados, pero no personlizados
No obstante, no te emociones demasiado. Esto no quiere decir que puedas añadir cualquier fondo animado a los chats, puesto que desde WAbetainfo destacan que es una selección muy específica con una velocidad de los movimientos de estas animaciones muy limitada. La idea es que estos fondos animados muestren un movimiento lento y gradual para que el fondo se perciba dinámico, pero sin desviar la atención de la conversación.
Además, los colores de las burbujas de chat variarán según el fondo de pantalla, pero será la app quien los seleccione automáticamente en lugar de permitir que los usuarios los personalicen por separado.
Sobre cuándo llegarán estas nuevas funcionalidades, es todo un misterio. Aún está en desarrollo y todavía no está ni siquiera disponible para los usuarios de la versión beta. Sin embargo, dado que WhatsApp está probando esta función tanto para iOS como para Android, es posible que veamos un lanzamiento más pronto que tarde para ambas plataformas, a diferencia de otras funcionalidades.

articles.title: CMF has managed to make cheap but good clip earbuds
articles.text:
Clip earbuds are an exercise in compromise. It’s an inherent aspect of their design — and physics. They can be more comfortable for people that don’t like something jammed in their ear, but sound response suffers. Ambient awareness is great because you can easily hear the sound around you, which means to hear your own music the buds need to be turned up and potentially leak sound out to your neighbors. For what they offer, they can also get pricey, with popular pairs from Bose, Sony, and Shokz reaching $200. The CMF Clip Pro, though, are under $100, and while they still have those compromises, they handle them well.
CMF’s clip earbuds hit the balance between cheap and good
The CMF Clip Pro are a very comfortable option for those that hate things in their ears.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
CMF Clip Pro
The Good
- Very comfortable
- Good sound from a clip earbud
- Great ambient awareness
The Bad
- 3-band EQ can be tricky to adjust
- Case controls are gimmicky
CMF is Nothing’s budget sub-brand, and because it tends to release earbuds in the $40–$60 range, I was expecting the same when I first heard about the Clip Pro. But instead, the Clip Pro are $99 — the same price as Nothing’s Ear 3A that just came out last month with more features (and also more issues). Only a few days after release and the Clip Pro are already on sale at $79, which puts them at the price I think they should be.
Comfort is the Clip Pro’s big advantage. The flexible band avoids any pinching around the helix, and I didn’t experience any discomfort with how the speaker orb or battery/control capsule sat in and behind my ear. A clip design is the best option for those that have trouble fitting earbuds in their ear canals.
Not having the sealed fit in your ear canals, though, affects the sound consistency, and I wouldn’t suggest doing any critical listening on the Clip Pro — or any clip earbuds, for that matter. Even so, the sound balance didn’t negatively affect my listening of my regular playlists and KCSN radio station app. By default, there’s a bass boost, which is necessary without a sealed fit but doesn’t cause the sound to be overly bassy (which other Nothing earbuds can be).
There’s a three-band EQ in the Nothing X app to adjust to taste, although as with other Nothing earbuds and headphones, the EQ can be tricky to use. Increasing a slider doesn’t always boost that frequency band, but instead lowers the other frequencies (increasing the bass, for example, actually brings down the mids and highs). It takes some getting used to and extra finagling. The Clip Pro support fixed spatial audio, which adds more space to the sound (I didn’t find it objectionable, but preferred the sound without it), as well as high-res audio over LDAC. The differences with high-res on an open-ear design are so minute, it’s not worth it, especially with any ambient noise around.
While listening to my radio app, the DJ’s voice could get difficult to understand during talk breaks with traffic going by. Boosting the volume can solve the problem, but it can also cause the sound to leak out to be heard by those close to you (benchmates on the bus or subway, for example). Turning on anti-leakage mode in the app cuts higher frequencies, but also adversely affects sound quality. The sound only leaks at high volumes, so it’s best to just turn them down.
There are multiple options for adjusting the volume in those situations, including directly from your device, with buttons on the capsules that rest behind each ear, or with a dial on the case (assignable in the app). The dial is also a button that can play and pause, skip forward and back, or call up your phone’s assistant.
There isn’t quite enough resistance to the dial, so at times while the case was in my pocket, volume would go up or down by a click or two. I ended up disabling the dial and either using the buttons on the earbuds, which work well although with a slight delay, or just pulling out my phone instead of the case. And with functionality disabled the dial becomes a great fidget toy.
The Clip Pro are pretty good with calls and don’t exhibit the buggy functionality I experienced with the Nothing Ear 3A, where the compression on my voice would drastically adjust based on the ambient sound when I started talking. The noise gate is still very aggressive to filter out any surrounding sound and can clip the very end of a word, but when I was speaking at normal volumes while walking down the street, my wife was able to understand me easily. Soft-spoken people might run into issues, though. When I spoke quietly, I sounded very muffled and it took her lots of concentration to try and figure out what I said.
That call quality epitomizes the CMF Clip Pro, and it’s the same with their sound. The earbuds are good at what they do under the constraints of the technology. And their comfort, along with their price, make them great when you don’t want something deep in your ear.
Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

articles.title: Efficient and Accurate Prediction of Cosite Isolation on Large Platforms - Wiley Science and Engineering Content Hub
articles.text:
Download this complimentary White Paper today!
This White Paper shows engineers and researchers how to predict, by simulation, the coupling between antennas mounted on electrically large platforms such as an airliner — and how to keep the results accurate even when the coupling is as low as -100 dB.
What you will learn about:
- Why platform size and coupling strength are two separate problems, and why the antenna pairs hidden from each other are the demanding case.
- How higher-order basis functions allow patches up to 2λ in size, reducing the number of unknowns compared with conventional low-order triangular meshing — and why the cubic cost of a direct solve makes every unknown you avoid pay back many times over.
- Why every numerical model of a closed metal platform behaves like a cavity, and how the spurious fields trapped inside it, not the platform itself, spoil low-level results.
- How to treat the reference frequency as a convergence test, so you can see when a coupling result has settled instead of assuming it.
- How absorbing material and air-filled ‘bubbles’ suppress spurious fields, allowing accurate low-level coupling results with fewer unknowns.
Click “LOOK INSIDE” to Download Now.
IEEE Spectrum and Wiley are proud to bring you this white paper, sponsored by WIPL‑D.
More Information
Aircraft, ships and vehicles now carry many radio systems in a small space, so designers must know how much energy leaks from one antenna into another before any hardware is built. This leakage is described by the mutual s-parameters between the antenna ports, and it decides whether two systems can operate at the same time on the same platform. Measuring it by trial and error at every candidate position is slow and costly. Predicting it by simulation is difficult for two reasons. First, the platform is electrically large, which means that its dimensions span several hundreds of wavelengths, so the model needs a large number of unknowns. Second, the coupling levels of interest are very low, in some cases down to -100 dB, which leaves little margin for numerical error. This White Paper addresses both problems with a full-wave solution based on the Method of Moments applied to the Surface Integral Equation, using higher-order basis functions to keep the number of unknowns low. Two examples are studied in detail: a metallic cube carrying two quarter-wavelength monopoles, and a realistic airliner carrying five monopoles at 1.06 GHz, where the fuselage is about 140 λ long. Three modelling techniques for obtaining accurate low-level results are compared in terms of accuracy and the number of unknowns each one requires, and the complete geometry of each model is documented so that every result can be checked independently.

articles.title: RingCentral data breach exposed info of 1.6 million accounts
articles.text:
The ShinyHunters extortion group stole personal information from 1.6 million RingCentral accounts after hacking the company in July, according to the data breach notification service Have I Been Pwned.
RingCentral is a cloud-based collaboration and communication platform used by over 600,000 businesses for services such as calling, messaging, and voicemail.
The company disclosed the incident on July 28, revealing that its systems were compromised following what it described as a "sophisticated social engineering campaign."
"We have not seen any new unauthorized activity since taking these remediation efforts. To date, this incident has affected data for a limited portion of RingCentral customers, and we are communicating with affected customers directly," it noted.
"If you are not contacted by RingCentral, you are not affected. This incident did not impact the core RingCentral platform, and our services continue to operate without disruption."
Although RingCentral has not attributed the breach to a specific threat actor or hacking group and has yet to share further details on the incident, the ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility on July 27, claiming they had stolen 623GB of data.
After the company refused to pay a ransom to have the stolen data destroyed, the cybercrime group leaked a compressed archive containing 280GB worth of files on their dark web leak site.
While a RingCentral spokesperson didn't immediately reply when contacted by BleepingComputer to confirm ShinyHunters' claims, Have I Been Pwned confirmed the link after analyzing the leaked data and said on Thursday that it contained records for 1.6 million accounts, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.
"In July 2026, the cloud-based business communications platform RingCentral was the target of a ShinyHunters 'pay or leak' extortion campaign," it said.
Although RingCentral has yet to share exactly how the threat actors gained access to its systems, ShinyHunters has claimed breaches at hundreds of Salesforce customers over the past year, saying they've stolen over 1.5 billion records in Salesloft Drift and Salesforce Aura campaigns.
The extortion group was also linked to security breaches at more than a dozen Snowflake customers, as well as various other third-party integration providers.
Most recently, ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for a new series of breaches at over 100 organizations following data-theft attacks that exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day flaw.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
